name: Gates of the Arctic National Park and Preserve
blurb: Caribou, wolves and tundra in a roadless Brooks Range wilderness.

tip.title: Remove the caribou
tip.text: Caribou feed wolves, bears and scavengers. Set Caribou to -100% and watch the wolf, grizzly, wolverine and raven, while lichen is left ungrazed.

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Gates of the Arctic National Park and Preserve, Reindeer, Brooks Range). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: Frozen ground lies just below a thin thawed surface layer. Warming has begun to thaw it, causing erosion and slope failures.
Cold, shallow soils hold limited nutrients that plants and decomposers recycle slowly.

nodes.name: Fungi and soil microbes
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants and carcasses, slowly in the cold, and return nutrients to the soil.
A pale ground lichen. Wikipedia says caribou dig through snow to reach it, and it is a winter staple for them.
Wikipedia describes migrations between taiga winter range and tundra summer range. The Western Arctic herd moves through the central Brooks Range and feeds wolves, bears and people.
A white mountain sheep of alpine slopes in the Brooks Range that grazes grasses and sedges.
Eats plants and some small animals, then hibernates through winter. GloBI records it as prey of grizzlies and wolverines.
A grouse that feeds on willow buds and twigs and other tundra plants. GloBI records it as prey of foxes, wolverines, grizzlies and stoats.
Eats rodents, birds and berries. GloBI records it feeding on voles, lemmings, ptarmigan and caribou.
A scavenging bird that feeds on carrion, berries and small animals, and stays all winter in the Arctic.
Hunts caribou, Dall sheep and smaller animals in the Brooks Range. A top predator of the caribou herds.

nodes.name: Grizzly bear
nodes.desc: The park has a low density of grizzlies, roughly one bear per 100 square miles. They eat berries, ground squirrels and caribou.

story: Gates of the Arctic National Park and Preserve in northern Alaska is the northernmost national park in the United States, entirely north of the Arctic Circle. It covers 8,472,506 acres of the central Brooks Range, and about 85% of it is wilderness. The wilderness area adjoins the Noatak Wilderness.
matters: Together they form the largest contiguous wilderness in the United States. Snowfields and glaciers that many ecosystems depend on are shrinking rapidly as temperatures rise.
